identity.name: Hands-on-Keyboard Behavioral Anomaly on a Service Account — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1059.004 / T1078.003 / T1046)
identity.summary: A Linux service account (svc-backup) whose learned Cortex profile is scheduled, non-interactive automation is driven interactively — the hands-on-keyboard tradecraft of Scattered Spider / Muddled Libra. No command is a known-bad IOC; the deviation from the account's learned baseline plus the causality chain is what an auto-tuned ABIOC anchors on and fires on.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the ENDPOINT plane — the gap where the corpus previously had only cloud/container ABIOC coverage. It models the signature hands-on-keyboard tradecraft attributed to Scattered Spider / Muddled Libra (UNC3944): after obtaining valid credentials for a low-noise service account, the operator works interactively on the host, running living-off-the-land discovery and staging tooling. Cortex has learned that svc-backup is an automation identity — it spawns a small, stable set of scheduled processes (tar, rsync, gzip) under cron, never an interactive shell, and never a fan-out of discovery utilities. The scenario injects two behavioral deviations from that learned baseline: (a) an interactive shell lineage (login-style bash -i with a controlling tty) attached to the automation account, and (b) a rapid burst of LOLBin discovery/staging (whoami, id, uname, hostname, ss, curl of an internal target) at a command cadence a backup job never exhibits. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad binary or command string would miss this — every binary used is a legitimate admin tool — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the account's learned behavior and anchors it to the causality chain (service-account auth -> interactive shell -> LOLBin discovery burst). Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the baseline identity and surfaces the interactive deviation; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single hands-on-keyboard-intrusion incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught novel activity no static rule was written for.

campaigns: Identity-driven hands-on-keyboard intrusions against enterprise SaaS and hybrid estates (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-010 — Hands-on-keyboard behavioral deviation on a learned automation account for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Linux agent installed on the target host so per-process and command telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed during which svc-backup ran only its scheduled, non-interactive jobs so Cortex learned the automation-identity profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads. Drive a learned automation account interactively and
# run a living-off-the-land discovery burst that deviates from its baseline.
set -euo pipefail
# (a) interactive shell lineage under the automation account
bash -ic 'echo "[CortexSim] interactive shell attached to automation account"' || true
# (b) LOLBin discovery/staging burst at a cadence a backup job never runs
for c in 'whoami' 'id' 'uname -a' 'hostname' 'ss -tunlp' 'cat /etc/passwd'; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
curl -s --max-time 5 "http://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/tool" -o /tmp/.stage 2>/dev/null || true

input_variables.name: STAGE_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised internal host the LOLBin staging curl reaches during the deviation.

expected_artifacts.description: An interactive shell (bash -i with a controlling tty) parented under the automation account whose learned baseline never spawns one.
A burst of living-off-the-land discovery utilities under the automation account within a short window.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_effective_username = "svc-backup" and action_process_image_name in (whoami, id, uname, hostname, ss)

abiocs.name: EDR-010 Anomalous Interactive Shell Lineage from Automation Account
abiocs.description: A service account whose learned Cortex behavioral profile is scheduled, non-interactive automation suddenly parents an interactive shell (login-style bash with a controlling tty). ABIOC anchors the deviation to the causality chain (service-account auth -> interactive shell) rather than to any known-bad binary, catching hands-on-keyboard use of a legitimate account that a static rule keyed on a bad command string would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "www-data", "nobody")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "zsh")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "-i" or action_process_command_line contains "login"
| comp count() as interactive_shells by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter interactive_shells >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, interactive_shells
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned automation-identity baseline (scheduled cron jobs, no interactive shell) -> service-account authentication -> interactive shell lineage that diverges from the baseline, anchored to the originating auth.

abiocs.name: EDR-010 Living-off-the-Land Discovery Burst Deviating from Account Baseline
abiocs.description: An automation account whose learned baseline is a narrow, repetitive process set runs a rapid burst of discovery/staging utilities (whoami, id, uname, hostname, ss, curl). Every utility is legitimate; the ABIOC fires on the cadence-and-diversity deviation from the account's learned behavior, anchored to the interactive shell that spawned them.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "www-data", "nobody")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("whoami", "id", "uname", "hostname", "ss", "netstat", "curl", "wget")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as distinct_tools by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter distinct_tools >= 4
| sort desc distinct_tools
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, distinct_tools
abiocs.causality_anchor: Interactive shell under the automation account -> rapid fan-out of distinct discovery/staging utilities that exceeds the account's learned process diversity, anchored to the spawning shell.

xql_queries.name: EDR-010 Automation Account Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter actor_effective_username = "svc-backup"
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as baseline_tools by agent_hostname
| filter baseline_tools >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, baseline_tools

xql_queries.name: EDR-010 Interactive Deviation Surfaced on Automation Account
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username = "svc-backup"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh")
| comp count() as interactive_spawns by agent_hostname
| filter interactive_spawns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, interactive_spawns

correlation_rules.name: Hands-on-Keyboard Intrusion on Automation Account — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(EDR-010 Anomalous Interactive Shell Lineage from Automation Account) AND ABIOC(EDR-010 Living-off-the-Land Discovery Burst Deviating from Account Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same host+account into a single hands-on-keyboard-intrusion incident anchored to the service-account causality chain.

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — auto-tuned behavioral profiling of per-identity process lineage and command cadence

products.evidence_query: Two ABIOCs fire on the automation-account behavioral deviation; CR-EDR-0010 stitches them into one hands-on-keyboard incident anchored to the service-account causality chain.
dataset = xdr_data | filter actor_effective_username = "svc-backup" | filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh")

use_cases.name: Hands-on-Keyboard Behavioral Anomaly Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a service account's non-interactive automation baseline and detect interactive hands-on-keyboard use of that account, anchored to its causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate binaries involved.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the svc-backup automation baseline and an injected interactive deviation fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex Linux agent installed.
Baseline window elapsed with svc-backup running only scheduled jobs.
steps: Let the automation baseline window elapse.
Attach an interactive shell to svc-backup and run a discovery burst.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-EDR-0010 raise a hands-on-keyboard incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `EDR-010 Anomalous Interactive Shell Lineage from Automation Account` fires.
ABIOC `EDR-010 Living-off-the-Land Discovery Burst Deviating from Account Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-EDR-0010 raises one stitched hands-on-keyboard-intrusion incident.

preventive_controls: Deny interactive shells for service/automation accounts (set login shell to /usr/sbin/nologin and enforce via PAM) so hands-on-keyboard use is blocked, not merely detected.
Scope service-account credentials tightly and rotate them; require phishing-resistant MFA for any interactive access path Scattered Spider abuses.
Alert on any tty-attached session for accounts whose baseline is non-interactive automation.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity process and command baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual LOLBins.
Alert on an automation account parenting an interactive shell lineage.
Alert on an account's process-diversity or command cadence exceeding its learned behavioral baseline.
